correctness.rationale: Every tree vertex has record mean reciprocal to its path size. Comparable-pair record indicators are independent via independent random permutation insertion ranks. For incomparable vertices, splitting the exact two-dimensional survival-value integral gives joint moment (1/(k+a)+1/(k+b))/(k+a+b) and covariance \(k/((k+a)(k+b)(k+a+b))>0\). This determines all depths, then each unique parent as the sole zero-covariance candidate on the preceding depth level. Uniform separation greater than \(\(1/(2n^3)\)\), Hoeffding concentration with \(\\(\eta=1/(24n^3)\)\), and union bound give error probability at most \(2n^2\exp(-N/(288n^6))\). The standard-library checker exhaustively enumerated rooted labeled trees \(n\le5\) with designated root zero and all mark ranks, plus seeded size-6 exhaustive and larger symbolic checks: 630088 exact assertions.

originality.rationale: The assessed claim is vertex-labeled inverse recovery from first and second moments of an observable full binary path-record vector, including an explicit high-probability sample bound. Classical path record means and dependence are explicitly credited, not claimed original. A search for the inverse claim and comparisons of relevant existing laws found no coverage. Remaining uninspected sections and earlier inverse-problem literature create a genuine priority risk; no uniqueness is inferred merely from search absence.
residual_risks: Not every section or appendix of Janson’s directly relevant 2004 preprint could be inspected; pairwise record identities or an equivalent inverse consequence could have appeared there.
Relevant earlier statistical tree-topology identification work might use different terminology and be absent from the searched literature.
The sufficient sample bound is not shown minimax optimal, and the theorem does not handle unstable or unobserved vertex identities.

value.rationale: Reconstructing an unknown labeled ancestry tree from repeated binary no/yes root-path record observations is a natural hidden-structure inference problem. The theorem identifies the exact minimal-order moments needed, proves identifiability for every finite branching shape, and supplies a universal finite-sample high-probability reconstruction rule. It meaningfully differs from scalar record count asymptotics and unlabelled polynomial tree invariants. The practical observation restrictions and nonoptimal sample bound are explicitly stated.
